title: Asteroid SE1 metadata: MPC-line parsing, config numbers, file loading
description:
# Asteroid SE1 metadata parsing + config + file loading

## Summary
Parse the MPC-elements line and asteroid name of individual-asteroid `.se1` files into per-file metadata (the stateless replacement for C's `swed.ast_H`/`ast_G`/`ast_diam`/`astnam` globals), add `EphemerisConfig::asteroid_numbers`, and load main-asteroid (`seas*`) + configured numbered-asteroid files in `Ephemeris::new`. Foundation for the whole asteroid arc — no calc dispatch yet.

## Files
- `src/sweph_file/types.rs` — new `AsteroidMeta` struct; new `asteroid: Option<AsteroidMeta>` field on `FileHeader`.
- `src/sweph_file/parse.rs` — MPC-line parsing (§3.2) + name extraction (§3.3); fix `detect_file_type` for 6-digit asteroid filenames.
- `src/sweph_file/mod.rs` — `asteroid_file_candidates` + `open_asteroid_file` helpers; re-export `AsteroidMeta`.
- `src/config.rs` — `pub asteroid_numbers: Vec<i32>` on `EphemerisConfig` (+ `Default`).
- `src/context.rs` — `main_asteroid_files: Vec<SwissEphFile>` + `asteroid_files: Vec<SwissEphFile>` fields on `Ephemeris`; loading in `new()`.

## Implementation steps
1. **`AsteroidMeta`** in `sweph_file/types.rs`: `pub struct AsteroidMeta { pub h: f64, pub g: f64, pub diameter_km: f64, pub name: String }`. Add `pub asteroid: Option<AsteroidMeta>` to `FileHeader` (always `None` for Planet/Moon/MainAsteroid/PlanetaryMoon files — C only populates these for `SEI_FILE_ANY_AST`, see c-ref-asteroid.md §4.3).
2. **MPC-line parse** in `parse.rs::parse_file`, `FileType::Asteroid` only (PlanetaryMoon keeps its 4-line skip, meta stays `None`). The 4th text line is currently just skipped by the line-counting loop — capture its bytes. Algorithm per c-ref-asteroid.md §3.2 (verified worked example there — Eros line included):
   - Compute `i`: skip leading spaces, skip ASCII digits, skip exactly one more byte. `i` = byte offset where the name begins.
   - `h = atof(line[35+i..])`, `g = atof(line[42+i..])`; if `g == 0.0` → `g = 0.15`.
   - Diameter: exactly the 7 bytes `line[51+i .. 51+i+7]` → atof; if `0.0` → `diameter_km = 1329.0 / 0.15_f64.sqrt() * 10f64.powf(-0.2 * h)`.
   - Write a small `fn atof_prefix(bytes: &[u8]) -> f64` helper matching C `atof`: skip leading whitespace, parse optional sign + digits + optional fraction (+ optional exponent), stop at first invalid byte, return 0.0 if nothing parses. Guard all slices — if the line is shorter than an offset, treat the field as 0.0.
3. **Name extraction** per §3.3: build `sastnam` = first `19 + i` bytes of the line. Re-parse the MPC number from it (`j = 4; while sastnam[j] != b' ' && j < 10 { j += 1 }`, number = the first `j` bytes as integer). If number `== ipl[0] - 10000` or `== ipl[0]`: name = up to 19 bytes of `sastnam[j+1..]`, and still skip the 30-byte field (cursor alignment). Else: name = the 30-byte field itself. Right-trim trailing spaces, then truncate at the first `"  "` (double space). NOTE the ordering constraint: the name decision needs `ipl[]`, which is read AFTER the text header — keep the raw MPC line bytes until then (the existing `r.skip(30)?` at parse.rs:158-160 is where the 30-byte consumption already happens; replace it with the conditional read).
4. **`detect_file_type` fix** (mod.rs:58-76): 6-digit asteroid files are named `s136108s.se1` (no `se` prefix — c-ref-asteroid.md §2.3), which currently falls to the error arm. Add: stem starts with `'s'` followed by an ASCII digit → `FileType::Asteroid`. Keep the existing `se` + digit branch.
5. **Path candidates** in mod.rs, per c-ref-asteroid.md §2.3 + §2.4 (exact 4-attempt retry order): `fn asteroid_file_candidates(dir: &Path, mpc: i32) -> [PathBuf; 4]`. Base name: `format!("se{mpc:05}")` for mpc ≤ 99999, `format!("s{mpc:06}")` for mpc > 99999. Subdir `ast{mpc/1000}`. Order: `astN/{base}.se1`, `astN/{base}s.se1`, `{base}.se1`, `{base}s.se1`. Then `pub fn open_asteroid_file(dir: &Path, mpc: i32) -> Result<SwissEphFile, Error>`: try each candidate with `SwissEphFile::open`, return first success; if all fail return `Error::FileNotFound(<first candidate path>)`.
6. **Config**: `pub asteroid_numbers: Vec<i32>` on `EphemerisConfig`, default empty. Doc comment: numbered asteroids to preload at construction; `Body::Asteroid(n)` calc requires `n` listed here (stateless design — no lazy file opening; caching/lazy-open is a dispatcher concern, swisseph-rs/6).
7. **Loading in `Ephemeris::new`** (context.rs:51-106): add the two `Vec<SwissEphFile>` fields. Asteroid files load whenever `config.ephe_path` is `Some(..)` — for ALL THREE ephemeris sources, not just Swiss (C reads asteroids from `.se1` regardless of epheflag, c-ref-asteroid.md §1.4; tasks B depends on this). `main_asteroid_files = open_ephemeris_files(dir, "seas")` but TOLERANT of absence: `open_ephemeris_files` errors only if the dir is unreadable; wrap so a missing/empty result yields an empty Vec (users without seas files must still construct fine — the error surfaces at calc time). For each deduplicated `n` in `config.asteroid_numbers`: `open_asteroid_file(dir, n)?` — hard error at construction (explicit config request → fail fast). No `ephe_path` + non-empty `asteroid_numbers` → `Error::FileFormat("ephe_path required for asteroid files")`.
8. **Tests** (unit, `#[cfg(test)]` in parse.rs/mod.rs):
   - Synthetic MPC-line fixture: build a minimal fake header? No — too much format scaffolding. Instead test the extracted parsing fn directly: factor the MPC-line → `AsteroidMeta`(minus name) logic into `fn parse_mpc_elements(line: &[u8]) -> (f64, f64, f64)` and unit-test it with the exact Eros line from c-ref-asteroid.md §3.2's worked example: expect `h == 10.38`, `g == 0.15`, `diameter_km == 1329.0 / 0.15_f64.sqrt() * 10f64.powf(-0.2 * 10.38)` (bitwise, same expression).
   - Integration test (skip-if-absent guard on the path): open `<repo>/ephe/ast0/se00433s.se1` (use `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")`): assert `header().file_type == FileType::Asteroid`, `planets()[0].body_id == 10433`, `header().time_range == (2268922.5, 2488522.5)`, meta `h == 10.38`, `g == 0.15`, `name == "Eros"`. Same for the 6-digit file `<repo>/ephe/ast136/s136199s.se1` (Eris): opens, `body_id == 146199`... CAREFUL: 10000 + 136199 = 146199. Assert `body_id == 146199` and `name` contains "Eris".
   - `Ephemeris::new` with `ephe_path = <repo>/ephe`, `asteroid_numbers: vec![433]` → Ok; with `vec![99999]` (no such file) → `Err(Error::FileNotFound(..))`.

## C reference
`docs/c-ref-asteroid.md` §2 (filename generation + retry order), §3 (exact MPC column arithmetic — includes a hex-verified worked example), §4.3 (why metadata must be per-file, not global). `docs/c-ref-se1-file.md` § read_const Steps 4/11 for surrounding context. Do NOT read the C source.

## Golden tests
No new golden JSON in this task — the numeric H/G/diam values get golden-verified end-to-end in the pheno task (attr[4]/attr[3] depend on them). Verification here = the unit/integration tests above + the existing suite staying green:
- `cargo test --test golden se1_header -- --nocapture` passes (existing)
- `cargo test -p swisseph` (unit tests incl. the new ones) passes

## Acceptance criteria
- `cargo test` passes (all existing + new unit tests)
- `cargo test --test golden` passes unchanged
- `cargo clippy --all-targets` introduces no new warnings
- `Ephemeris::new` behavior per step 7/8 verified by tests

## Escape hatch
If the Eros/Eris integration assertions fail after two debugging attempts (wrong h/g/diam/name/body_id), STOP and report: which field, expected vs actual, and the raw line bytes. Do not guess at column offsets beyond what §3.2 specifies — escalate to Opus.
execution_record: Implemented in a single commit, all 8 steps per plan. No surprises — Eros (se00433s.se1) and Eris (s136199s.se1) integration tests passed on first attempt with correct H/G/name values. The MPC line capture required changing parse_file's text-header loop from a simple skip to index-aware capture (line_idx==3 for Asteroid type). The 30-byte name field skip was restructured from a blanket Asteroid|PlanetaryMoon guard into two branches: Asteroid parses it via extract_asteroid_name, PlanetaryMoon still skips. Clippy caught identical if-block arms in detect_file_type; merged into a single || condition.

messages.text: Codex review: needs-attention → fixed (2f911dc). Two medium findings: (1) older-format asteroid name fallback was discarded instead of reading the 30-byte field — fixed by passing name_field_30 into extract_asteroid_name; (2) open_asteroid_file retry loop swallowed all errors instead of only FileNotFound — fixed with explicit match arm.
